battle.name: 亞美尼亞-安息戰爭
battle.theater: 米底高原與幼發拉底上游
battle.brief: 前八十七年，亞美尼亞王梯格拉尼斯二世再入米底，安息王帕科魯斯一世在塞琉古王安提奧庫斯四世協助下迎戰，於里帕克河一役重創亞軍，迫使梯格拉尼斯退守提格拉諾塞爾達。卡面的亞述長矛早此戰八百餘年，它真正延續下來的不是標槍，而是方陣與重騎兵手中那柄抵住前列的長矛。

kit.name: 亞述長矛
kit.history: 短柄、長刃，配著鐵鏃。亞述人把它和弓、鐵器綁在一起，兩河流域的城一個接一個陷落。

countries: 亞美尼亞-安息戰爭爆發於公元前八十七年，是亞美尼亞王國與安息（帕提亞）王國之間的一場直接衝突，交戰重心在米底、索菲尼與幼發拉底上游一帶。亞美尼亞一方是阿爾塔克亞斯王朝，國王梯格拉尼斯二世（Tigranes II）自亞美尼亞高原出動，軍隊以希臘化方陣步兵為骨幹，配塞種、高加索與阿拉伯式輕騎兵、投射兵、工兵與攻城器材，前線自索菲尼一路推到巴比倫、蘇薩與埃科巴塔納。安息一方是阿爾薩息王朝，國王帕科魯斯一世（Pacorus I）坐鎮安息與兩河中下游，軍隊以弓騎兵與披重甲的鐵甲騎兵為主，輔以柳條盾步兵、投射兵與象兵殘部，米底、索菲尼與美索不達米亞北部都在其勢力範圍之內。第三方是塞琉古王國：國王安提奧庫斯四世（Antiochus IV）以協助安息、收復失土為名，出兵並出資把米底與巴比倫方向的戰線拉開，使安息得以集中兵力對付梯格拉尼斯。雙方都沒有留下可核對的完整編制，交戰規模只能從戰報殘篇與後世史家的量級描述推斷。
countriesEn: The Armenian-Parthian War broke out in 87 BC as a direct clash between the Kingdom of Armenia and the Parthian kingdom, with the fighting centred on Media, Sophene and the upper Euphrates. On the Armenian side stood the Artaxiad dynasty under King Tigranes II, who marched out of the Armenian highlands with an army whose backbone was Hellenised phalanx infantry, supported by Saka, Caucasian and Arab light cavalry, missile troops, engineers and siege equipment; his front line had reached Babylon, Susa and Ecbatana. On the Parthian side was the Arsacid dynasty under King Pacorus I, based at Parthia and along the middle and lower Euphrates, whose army was built on horse archers and heavily armoured cataphracts, supported by gerrha-shield infantry, missile troops and the remains of elephant units; Media, Sophene and northern Mesopotamia all lay inside his sphere. A third party was the Seleucid kingdom: King Antiochus IV intervened in the name of aiding Parthia and recovering lost territory, supplying troops, trainers and money so that Parthia could concentrate its forces against Tigranes. Neither side left a complete order of battle that can be checked, so the scale of the clash has to be inferred from fragments of battle narrative and from the rough magnitudes given by later historians.
people: 核心人物是亞美尼亞國王梯格拉尼斯二世。他約在公元前九十五年前後即位，藉著吞併索菲尼、擊敗塞琉古與米底勢力的機會，把王國從高原推向兩河，前八十八年一度奪下巴比倫與蘇薩。他早年曾與安息王米特里達梯二世聯姻，此後卻把姻親的勢力範圍一步步吃掉，聯姻反而成了交戰的起點之一。另一方是安息王帕科魯斯一世，米特里達梯二世之子，長期在美索不達米亞與敘利亞作戰，前八十八年同塞琉古聯軍擊潰梯格拉尼斯的一支大軍，前八十七年親自率軍在里帕克河擊敗梯格拉尼斯本人。塞琉古王安提奧庫斯四世是關鍵的第三方，他提供兵員、教練與軍資，換取安息對塞琉古邊境施壓，事後又趁安息得勝收回巴比倫。留下戰況細節的是史家：梅米烏斯（Memmius）的殘篇經蓋路斯（Aulus Gellius）《阿提卡夜話》第五卷保存，卡西烏斯·狄奧（Cassius Dio）亦留下相關記述，後世史家多據此還原這場戰爭。值得注意的是帕科魯斯的結局：前五十三年他在卡里（Carrhae）被羅馬將領卡修斯擊殺身死，與梯格拉尼斯同為終身勁敵的兩個人，先後在同一條戰線上碰頭。
peopleEn: The central figure is King Tigranes II of Armenia. He took the throne around 95 BC and, seizing the chance offered by the annexation of Sophene and the defeat of Seleucid and Median forces, pushed his kingdom out of the highlands and down the two rivers; in 88 BC he seized Babylon and Susa outright. He had earlier married into the Parthian dynasty, taking a daughter of Mithridates II, and then proceeded to swallow his in-laws' sphere of influence piece by piece, so that the marriage itself became one of the causes of the war. On the other side stands King Pacorus I of Parthia, son of Mithridates II, who had campaigned for years in Mesopotamia and Syria; in 88 BC he and the Seleucids broke an Armenian army, and in 87 BC he led his own force against Tigranes personally at the Rypax and won. Antiochus IV of Seleucia was the decisive third party: he provided men, drill instructors and money, and in exchange pressed on Parthia's borders, afterwards recovering Babylon while Parthia was carrying the war. The details of the fighting survive because of the historians: fragments of Memmius were preserved by Aulus Gellius in the fifth book of the Attic Nights, and Cassius Dio left a related account, on which most modern reconstructions rest. The fate of Pacorus deserves a note: in 53 BC he was killed at Carrhae by the Roman general Cassius, so the two men who were each other's lifelong rivals met on the same front in turn.
kits: 卡面這柄亞述長矛，屬於公元前九至七世紀亞述帝國的標準步兵裝備：短柄、長刃、鐵鏃，配圓盾與短弓，密集隊形中矛尖斜舉成一片，用來頂住正面來敵。到公元前八十七年，亞述國家已滅去八百多年，這種制式武器本身不在任何軍隊的裝備表上，卡面與戰役屬於年代差而非戰場同框。它真正留下的痕跡是形制的延續：希臘化世界用來支撐方陣的薩里沙長槍（sarissa），以及安息與亞美尼亞重騎兵肩抵的長矛，都是同一條技術路線的後代——長柄、長鐵刃、重心前移，衝鋒時靠馬速把質量送進人體。戰場上真正決定勝負的裝備另有其物：安息方以複合弓配馳射之術，騎手在奔馳中回身放箭，再以鐵甲騎兵集群衝鋒，人馬皆披鱗甲或札甲，配柳條盾；亞美尼亞方是持薩里沙或短矛的方陣步兵、塞種輕騎兵的長矛與勾刀，以及大量投射兵。攻城方面，兩河流域城市設有守城砲與投石機，圍城方需要攻城塔與坑道，糧秣則靠車隊沿幼發拉底與底格里斯河輸送。
kitsEn: The Assyrian spear on the card was standard infantry equipment of the Assyrian empire between the ninth and seventh centuries BC: a short haft, a long blade and an iron head, carried with a round shield and a short bow, its points raised at a slant in dense order to hold off an enemy coming head-on. By 87 BC the Assyrian state had been gone for more than eight centuries, and this weapon in its original form appeared on no army's inventory; the card and the battle belong to different ages rather than to the same field. What it does leave behind is a line of design: the sarissa that supported the Hellenistic phalanx, and the shoulder-braced lance of the Parthian and Armenian heavy cavalry, are all heirs of the same technical path, with a long haft, a long iron blade and the centre of gravity moved forward, so that in the charge the speed of the horse carries the mass into the target. The equipment that actually decided the field lay elsewhere: Parthia fought with the composite bow and the shot taken at speed, the archer turning in the saddle at full gallop, and then with massed cataphracts whose horses and riders were protected by scale or lamellar armour, with wicker shields; Armenia fielded phalanx infantry carrying sarissas or short spears, Saka light cavalry with lance and gada, and a large body of missile troops. On the siege side, the Mesopotamian cities mounted stone-throwing engines and defending artillery, the besiegers needed towers and mine galleries, and grain moved to the armies on wagons along the Euphrates and the Tigris.
tactics: 亞述長矛的老規矩在這場戰爭裡只能作為結構上的對照：亞述方陣以多排縱深握矛待戰，號令一下同時刺出，把整面矛牆推成一個整體；公元前九世紀的這套做法，在希臘化世界換成長柄薩里沙之後仍然成立，亞美尼亞的方陣步兵沿用的正是同一原理。安息與塞琉古聯軍的部署則是典型的高原進攻解法：先以弓騎兵在遠距離消耗，邊打邊退，把追出隘口的亞美尼亞騎兵拉散，再用重甲騎兵在寬闊處集群衝鋒把人壓回去。里帕克河一役的具體過程沒有留下詳細記載，只能由結果倒推：安息方掌握了主動，把亞軍引入可展開的地帶，打斷其縱深，亞軍崩潰後梯格拉尼斯只帶走殘部退回首都。地形是關鍵——米底山地與幼發拉底上游的河谷階地，能讓弓騎兵周旋，卻讓重裝步兵難以維持正面寬度；一旦亞軍的方陣被側翼迂迴，長矛的優勢便被長矛的長度反噬。補給上，亞美尼亞遠征依賴幼發拉底與底格里斯河沿岸的糧倉，失敗一旦發生在遠離基地的一側，撤退本身就會變成第二次損失。
tacticsEn: The old drill of the Assyrian spear can serve here only as a structural comparison. The Assyrian phalanx held its spears in depth, ready, and on the signal thrust as one body, turning a wall of points into a single moving front; what that drill achieved in the ninth century BC, carried into the Hellenistic world on a longer haft, was still valid, and the Armenian phalanx infantry followed exactly the same principle. The deployment of the Parthian-Seleucid allied army is the standard solution for an advance into the highlands: horse archers opened at long range, giving ground as they shot to pull the Armenian cavalry out of the defile and stretch it out, and then the armoured heavy cavalry charged in mass where there was room to swing. No detailed account of the battle on the Rypax survives, so the sequence has to be reconstructed backwards from its result: the Parthians held the initiative, drew the Armenian army into ground where it could deploy, broke up its depth, and once the Armenian line collapsed Tigranes took only the remnant back to his capital. Terrain was decisive. The hills of Media and the terraces above the upper Euphrates allowed the horse archers to wheel and stay in contact, while heavy infantry could not hold a front wide enough; once the Armenian flank was turned, the same length of the spear that had protected it turned against it. On logistics, the Armenian expedition drew its grain from depots along the Euphrates and Tigris, and a defeat fought far from those depots turned the retreat itself into a second loss.
data: 時間上，這場戰爭的前哨是公元前八十八年：梯格拉尼斯奪下巴比倫與蘇薩，安提奧庫斯四世把巴比倫收復，聯軍在米底方向擊潰亞軍一部，決戰則在次年，即公元前八十七年。戰報殘篇留下的損失數字是全場最硬的資料：亞軍在里帕克河一役中損失約九千騎兵與七千步兵，梯格拉尼斯僅率數千騎兵退回提格拉諾塞爾達。這些數字來自梅米烏斯殘篇，敵方帳目難免誇大，讀時要留出餘地。雙方總兵力沒有可靠記載，只能借別處比對：普魯塔克記述前六十九年梯格拉尼斯面對盧庫盧斯時擁有十萬量級步兵與五千騎兵，說明這位國王十八年後仍有可觀的兵源；安息方面的騎兵規模，古代作家習慣以數萬形容，具體數字不見於殘篇。距離與地理方面，從亞美尼亞首都提格拉諾塞爾達到巴比倫約一千二百公里，到埃科巴塔納約八百公里；里帕克河的具體位置至今沒有定論，一般認為在米底境內、今伊拉克與伊朗交界的山區，本卡取米底高原東部為標記。作戰季節方面，此地秋季乾燥、夏季酷熱，最適宜的戰役窗口是夏末至初秋，本卡取九月為開戰月份。
dataEn: Chronologically, the opening moves of this war belong to 88 BC: Tigranes took Babylon and Susa, Antiochus IV recovered Babylon, the allied army broke an Armenian detachment in the direction of Media, and the decisive battle came the following year, in 87 BC. The hardest figures in the whole file are the losses preserved in the battle narrative: the Armenian army is said to have lost about nine thousand horsemen and seven thousand foot soldiers at the Rypax, and Tigranes returned to Tigranocerta with only a few thousand cavalry still with him. These figures come from the fragments of Memmius, and an enemy's figures should always be read with room to spare. Reliable totals for the two armies do not exist and can only be reached by comparison elsewhere: Plutarch describes Tigranes as fielding upwards of a hundred thousand foot and five thousand horse against Lucullus in 69 BC, which shows that the king could still draw on substantial manpower eighteen years later; the size of the Parthian cavalry is the sort of thing ancient writers habitually put at tens of thousands, and no exact number appears in the fragments. On distance and geography, the march from the Armenian capital Tigranocerta to Babylon is about twelve hundred kilometres, and to Ecbatana about eight hundred; the exact position of the Rypax has never been settled, and it is generally placed in Media, in the highlands along today's border between Iraq and Iran, so this card marks the eastern Media highlands. On the campaigning season, the country is dry in autumn and brutally hot in summer, which puts the best window at the turn of summer into early autumn; this card therefore takes September as the opening month.
cause: 交戰不是偶然擦槍，而是一連串擴張撞上另一個帝國的必然。前八十八年前後，梯格拉尼斯把亞美尼亞王國推成橫跨高原與兩河的陸權：他吞下索菲尼，攻入米底，奪取巴比倫、蘇薩與埃科巴塔納，等於同時向塞琉古與安息兩個勢力圈伸手。安息王權在米特里達梯二世手上已把索菲尼與幼發拉底上游從塞琉古手中奪過，如今自己的腹地與邊境被直接推進的亞美尼亞軍隊威脅，必須反擊；帕科魯斯一世又長期以敘利亞為目標，任何能削弱亞美尼亞的聯盟都值得拉攏。塞琉古王安提奧庫斯四世的算盤更直接：亞美尼亞占著他的米底與巴比倫，與安息開打，兩邊消耗，他便可趁勢收回巴比倫並把邊界推回幼發拉底。婚姻關係同樣是變數：梯格拉尼斯早年娶安息王女，後來卻把姻親的領地與附庸一併吞下，等於公開撕毀協議。於是三方在公元前八十八年形成了一條臨時軸線，導火索是梯格拉尼斯越境再入米底、深入安息腹地。
causeEn: The clash was no accidental brush between neighbours but the certain collision of one empire's expansion with another. Around 88 BC Tigranes turned the Armenian kingdom into a land power stretching from the highlands to the two rivers: he annexed Sophene, drove into Media, and took Babylon, Susa and Ecbatana, which meant reaching into the spheres of both Seleucia and Parthia at once. The Parthian kingship, which under Mithridates II had already taken Sophene and the upper Euphrates from the Seleucids, now saw its own heartland and frontier threatened by an army advancing out of Armenia, and had to answer; Pacorus I had long aimed at Syria, and any alliance that weakened Armenia was worth courting. The Seleucid king's calculation was more direct: Armenia held his Media and his Babylon, and while the two sides fought, both would be worn down, leaving him free to recover Babylon and push the frontier back to the Euphrates. Marriage was a variable in this as well. Tigranes had married a Parthian princess, and then annexed her relatives' lands and clients, which amounted to tearing up the agreement in public. So a temporary axis of three powers formed in 88 BC, and the trigger was Tigranes crossing the border again, marching into Media and deep into Parthian territory.
impact: 這一役的直接後果是亞美尼亞的西進方案被打斷，但被打斷的只是亞洲方向，梯格拉尼斯本人並未垮台。退回高原之後，他把軍力轉向小亞細亞與地中海東岸，前八十年代在比提尼亞、卡帕多西亞與奇里乞亞一連取得大勝，首都提格拉諾塞爾達的宏偉宮殿與他萬王之王的稱號也在這段日子裡定型。然而安息由此坐穩兩河與米底，前八十七年至前五十三年帕科魯斯及其後繼者不斷西征敘利亞，安息騎兵的身影開始出現在安提阿與奇里乞亞海岸，與塞琉古及後來的羅馬在東地中海對峙。塞琉古王國勉強復國，收回巴比倫卻元氣大傷，安提奧庫斯四世在公元前八十七年死於巴比倫，此後再無力重奪米底。從更長的視角看，這場戰爭替兩位主角都安排好了對手：梯格拉尼斯在公元前六十七年被龐培貶為羅馬的附庸，帕科魯斯在公元前五十三年卡里戰役中被卡修斯全殲，安息與羅馬的正面對抗從此成為帝國東翼的主題。
impactEn: The immediate effect of the battle was to interrupt the Armenian advance, but only in the Asian direction; Tigranes himself did not collapse. Back on the plateau, he turned his army towards Asia Minor and the eastern Mediterranean, and in the eighties took a run of clear victories in Bithynia, Cappadocia and Cilicia, while the great palace complex of Tigranocerta and his title of King of Kings took their final shape. Parthia, meanwhile, sat securely over the two rivers and Media, and from 87 BC to 53 BC Pacorus and his successors campaigned west into Syria, the Parthian horse appearing around Antioch and along the Cilician coast, to face the Seleucids and then the Romans across the eastern Mediterranean. The Seleucid kingdom survived, recovered Babylon, and was left exhausted; Antiochus IV died at Babylon in 87 BC, and the state never recovered Media. Seen from further back, this war arranged the future of both protagonists: Tigranes was demoted by Pompey to a client of Rome in 67 BC, and Pacorus was destroyed by Cassius at Carrhae in 53 BC; from then on the confrontation between Parthia and Rome became the standing theme of the eastern empire.
result: 公元前八十七年，帕科魯斯一世在里帕克河取得完勝：亞美尼亞軍隊在會戰中崩潰，梯格拉尼斯損失九千騎兵與七千步兵，只帶走數千騎兵退回提格拉諾塞爾達，亞軍的攻勢自此中止。安息保住了米底與索菲尼，幼發拉底上游重新回到其控制之下，剛被塞琉古收復的巴比倫也暫時免於再失。塞琉古王安提奧庫斯四世成了實際受益者，他在同一年重返巴比倫，但再沒有能力把亞美尼亞的勢力從西北趕出去。對亞美尼亞而言，這是一場敗仗而非崩潰：梯格拉尼斯退回亞美尼亞高原，之後轉向比提尼亞與卡帕多西亞，在他生涯最後二十年裡贏下多場更漂亮的戰役，前八十五年甚至攻入小亞細亞，把國勢推到與羅馬正面碰撞的距離。因此這場戰爭的結果要分兩層看：安息在安息與亞美尼亞的較勁中完勝，亞美尼亞的亞洲帝國計劃破產；可是戰敗的國王本人把失敗的代價轉嫁到西方，兩國的戰爭從此換了戰場，直到羅馬先後把梯格拉尼斯與帕科魯斯都拉進自己的計畫裡才真正收場。
resultEn: In 87 BC Pacorus I won a complete victory on the Rypax. The Armenian army collapsed in the engagement, Tigranes lost nine thousand horsemen and seven thousand foot soldiers and returned to Tigranocerta with only a few thousand cavalry, and the Armenian offensive stopped there. Parthia kept Media and Sophene, the upper Euphrates came back under its control, and Babylon, which the Seleucids had just retaken, was spared for the time being. Antiochus IV of Seleucia was the real beneficiary and returned to Babylon the same year, but he never had the strength to drive Armenian influence back out of the north-west. For Armenia this was a defeat rather than a collapse: Tigranes withdrew to the Armenian plateau and turned towards Bithynia and Cappadocia, winning several far more impressive battles in the last twenty years of his life and pushing as far as Asia Minor in 85 BC, close enough to Rome to collide with it. The result therefore has to be read on two levels. Parthia won the contest between the two of them outright, and the Armenian plan for an Asian empire collapsed; but the defeated king passed the cost of his defeat to the west, and the war between the two kingdoms moved to another front, where it was settled only when Rome drew first Tigranes and then Pacorus into its own plans.
